title: 'Not-quite primordial' black holes may explain baffling JWST discovery | New Scientist
description: The James Webb Space Telescope seems to have discovered more ancient black holes than theory had predicted, and now we have a new way to explain why
author: Matt von Hippel

title: Saturn has a big, weird decagon around its south pole | New Scientist
description: A decagon – a geometric polygon with 10 sides and 10 angles – has been found on Saturn, and nobody is quite sure how it got there
author: Jonathan O’Callaghan

title: Venus may have had a moon for nearly 2 billion years | New Scientist
description: A moon may once have been consumed by Venus, after existing alongside the planet for up to 1.7 billion years
author: Jonathan O’Callaghan

title: A nuclear reactor is being installed a mile underground in Kansas | New Scientist
description: Deep Fission has just received safety approval from the US Department of Energy for a reactor design that it plans to install at the bottom of a deep hole
author: Vanessa Bates Ramirez

title: Groundbreaking laser of ghostly particles may be impossible to build | New Scientist
description: A year ago, researchers made a splash with a wildly creative idea for building a laser from notoriously elusive particles, but a new analysis shows this is probably impossible
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Can we really reverse global warming after overshooting 1.5°C? | New Scientist
description: A UN report says it’s possible to get global temperatures back down to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels by the end of the century, but many researchers regard this scenario as highly unlikely
author: Michael Le Page
